--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.
**Built with GitHub Actions, OpenCode, shared skills, and unreasonable optimism.** 😏

/**
 * Level catalogue for CIRCUIT MASTER.
 *
 * Every level is authored as a real circuit. The `solutionWires` and
 * `solutionSwitches` fields are used by the hint system and by the automated
 * engine tests, not by validation (players may find an equivalent circuit).
 */

const AMBER = '#ffb84d'
const CYAN = '#4de8ff'
const MINT = '#5dffa8'
const ROSE = '#ff6f9f'
const VIOLET = '#b38cff'
const LIME = '#d7ff5f'

function led(id, x, y, color = AMBER) {
  return { id, type: 'led', x, y, color }
}

function sw(id, x, y, initial = false) {
  return { id, type: 'switch', x, y, initial }
}

function gate(id, type, x, y) {
  return { id, type, x, y }
}

function battery(id, x, y) {
  return { id, type: 'battery', x, y }
}

function w(a, b) {
  return { a, b }
}

+    hoveredPort = port.ref
+    elements.canvasWrap.classList.add('dragging')
+    try {
+      canvas.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)
+    } catch {
+      // Pointer capture is a progressive enhancement.
+    }
+    return
+  }
+
+  const switchComponent = board.switchAt(point.x, point.y)
+  if (switchComponent) {
+    armedPort = null
+    selectedWire = null
+    toggleSwitch(switchComponent)
+    return
+  }
+
+  const wireIndex = board.wireAt(point.x, point.y, state.wires, 16)
+  if (wireIndex !== null) {
+    armedPort = null
+    if (selectedWire === wireIndex) {
+      removeWire(wireIndex)
+      showToast('Wire cut')
+    } else {
+      selectedWire = wireIndex
+      sound.click()
+      showToast('Wire selected · tap it again to cut', '', 2400)
+    }
+    return
+  }
+
+  const component = board.componentAt(point.x, point.y)
+  if (component) {
+    armedPort = null
+    selectedWire = null
+    describeComponent(component)
+    sound.click()
+    return
+  }
+
+  selectedWire = null
+  if (armedPort) {
+    armedPort = null
+    showToast('Terminal disarmed')
+  }
+}
+
+function handlePointerMove(event) {
+  const point = pointerPosition(event)
+  if (drag) {
+    drag.point = point
+    drag.moved =
+      drag.moved || Math.hypot(point.x - drag.start.x, point.y - drag.start.y) > 8
+    const target = board.portAt(point.x, point.y, 36)
+    const valid =
+      target &&
+      target.ref !== drag.from &&
+      target.component.id !== drag.from.split(':')[0]
+    drag.targetRef = valid ? target.ref : null
+    hoveredPort = drag.targetRef || drag.from
+    hoveredSwitch = null
+    hoveredWire = null
+    return
+  }
+  hoverAt(point)
+}
+
+function finishPointerDrag(event, cancelled = false) {
+  if (!drag) return
+  const dragValue = drag
+  const target = dragValue.targetRef
+    ? board.portByRef.get(dragValue.targetRef)
+    : board.portAt(dragValue.point.x, dragValue.point.y, 36)
+  drag = null
+  elements.canvasWrap.classList.remove('dragging')
+  try {
+    canvas.releasePointerCapture(event.pointerId)
+  } catch {
+    // Ignore browsers that already released the pointer.
+  }
+  if (cancelled) {
+    armedPort = null
+    return
+  }
+  if (
+    target &&
+    target.ref !== dragValue.from &&
+    target.component.id !== dragValue.from.split(':')[0]
+  ) {
+    addWire(dragValue.from, target.ref)
+    return
+  }
+  if (!dragValue.moved) {
+    if (armedPort === dragValue.from) {
+      armedPort = null
+      showToast('Terminal disarmed')
+      sound.click()
+    } else {
+      armedPort = dragValue.from
+      sound.click()
+      showToast('Terminal armed · tap another terminal to connect', '', 3000)
+    }
+  }
+  hoveredPort = null
+}
+
+/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+/*  keyboard shortcuts                                                        */
+/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+
+function handleKeydown(event) {
+  if (event.target instanceof HTMLInputElement || event.target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement) return
+  const key = event.key.toLowerCase()
+  if (key === 'escape') {
+    if (drag) {
+      drag = null
+      elements.canvasWrap.classList.remove('dragging')
+      return
+    }
+    if (armedPort) {
+      armedPort = null
+      return
+    }
+    if (cutMode) {
+      toggleCutMode(false)
+      return
+    }
+    if (document.querySelector('dialog[open]')) return
+    selectedWire = null
+    return
+  }
+  if (document.querySelector('dialog[open]')) return
+  if (key === 'h' && !event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey) {
+    event.preventDefault()
+    useHint()
+  } else if (key === 'u' && !event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey) {
+    event.preventDefault()
+    undo()
+  } else if (key === 'r' && !event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey) {
+    event.preventDefault()
+    resetCurrentLevel()
+  } else if ((key === 'delete' || key === 'backspace') && selectedWire !== null) {
+    event.preventDefault()
+    removeWire(selectedWire)
+  } else if (key === 'c' && !event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey) {
+    toggleCutMode()
+  }
+}
+
+/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+/*  canvas loop                                                               */
+/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+
+function frame(time) {
+  board.draw({
+    time,
+    state,
+    sim: validation.sim,
+    loadAt,
+    hoveredPort,
+    hoveredSwitch,
+    hoveredWire,
+    selectedWire,
+    drag,
+    armedPort,
+    hint,
+    celebration,
+  })
+  requestAnimationFrame(frame)
+}
+
+/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+/*  level-modal reset                                                         */
+/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+
+let resetProgressArmed = false
+let resetProgressTimer = 0
+
+function resetCampaign() {
+  if (!resetProgressArmed) {
+    resetProgressArmed = true
+    elements.resetProgressButton.textContent = 'Confirm reset — this clears all progress'
+    clearTimeout(resetProgressTimer)
+    resetProgressTimer = window.setTimeout(() => {
+      resetProgressArmed = false
+      elements.resetProgressButton.textContent = 'Reset campaign'
+    }, 4200)
+    return
+  }
+  clearTimeout(resetProgressTimer)
+  resetProgressArmed = false
+  progress.completed = {}
+  progress.lastLevel = 1
+  saveProgress()
+  try {
+    localStorage.removeItem(SESSION_KEY)
+  } catch {
+    // Ignore unavailable storage.
+  }
+  elements.resetProgressButton.textContent = 'Campaign reset'
+  elements.levelModal.close()
+  setCurrentLevel(1, { fresh: true, saveCurrent: false })
+  showToast('Campaign reset · all 30 circuits available from the start', '', 3200)
+}
+
+/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+/*  init & events                                                             */
+/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+
+function bindEvents() {
+  canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown', handlePointerDown)
+  canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', handlePointerMove)
+  canvas.addEventListener('pointerup', (event) => finishPointerDrag(event, false))
+  canvas.addEventListener('pointercancel', (event) => finishPointerDrag(event, true))
+  canvas.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => {
+    if (!drag) {
+      hoveredPort = null
+      hoveredSwitch = null
+      hoveredWire = null
+    }
+  })
+  canvas.addEventListener('contextmenu', (event) => {
+    event.preventDefault()
+    const point = pointerPosition(event)
+    const wireIndex = board.wireAt(point.x, point.y, state.wires, 16)
+    if (wireIndex !== null) {
+      removeWire(wireIndex)
+      showToast('Wire cut')
+    }
+  })
+
+  elements.levelsButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
+    sound.click()
+    renderLevelGrid()
+    updateCampaignUI()
+    openDialog(elements.levelModal)
+  })
+
+  elements.helpButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
+    sound.click()
+    openDialog(elements.helpModal)
+  })
+
+  elements.soundButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
+    sound.ensure()
+    setSoundMuted(!progress.muted)
+    if (!progress.muted) sound.unlock()
+  })
+
+  elements.hintButton.addEventListener('click', useHint)
+  elements.undoButton.addEventListener('click', undo)
+  elements.cutButton.addEventListener('click', () => toggleCutMode())
+  elements.cutButtonTop.addEventListener('click', () => toggleCutMode())
+  elements.resetButton.addEventListener('click', () => resetCurrentLevel())
+  elements.nextLevelButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
+    if (level.id >= LEVEL_COUNT) {
+      openDialog(elements.levelModal)
+      renderLevelGrid()
+      return
+    }
+    if (!isUnlocked(level.id + 1)) {
+      showToast(`Complete level ${pad(level.id)} to unlock level ${pad(level.id + 1)}`, 'danger')
+      return
+    }
+    sound.click()
+    setCurrentLevel(level.id + 1)
+  })
+
+  elements.levelModal.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
+    const card = event.target.closest('.level-card')
+    if (card) {
+      const id = Number(card.dataset.level)
+      if (!isUnlocked(id)) {
+        showToast(`Level ${pad(id)} is locked · complete level ${pad(id - 1)} first`, 'danger')
+        sound.error()
+        return
+      }
+      sound.click()
+      elements.levelModal.close()
+      setCurrentLevel(id)
+      if (window.matchMedia('(max-width: 980px)').matches) {
+        window.setTimeout(() => {
+          elements.canvasWrap.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center' })
+        }, 90)
+      }
+      return
+    }
+    if (event.target === elements.levelModal) elements.levelModal.close()
+  })
+
+  elements.helpModal.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
+    if (event.target === elements.helpModal) elements.helpModal.close()
+  })
+  elements.completeModal.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
+    if (event.target === elements.completeModal) elements.completeModal.close()
+  })
+
+  document.querySelectorAll('[data-close]').forEach((button) => {
+    button.addEventListener('click', () => {
+      const dialog = button.closest('dialog')
+      if (dialog) closeDialog(dialog)
+    })
+  })
+
+  elements.resetProgressButton.addEventListener('click', resetCampaign)
+
+  elements.nextButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
+    elements.completeModal.close()
+    if (level.id >= LEVEL_COUNT) {
+      renderLevelGrid()
+      updateCampaignUI()
+      openDialog(elements.levelModal)
+      return
+    }
+    setCurrentLevel(level.id + 1, { fresh: true })
+    sound.click()
+  })
+
+  elements.replayButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
+    elements.completeModal.close()
+    setCurrentLevel(level.id, { fresh: true })
+    sound.click()
+  })
+
+  elements.completeMapButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
+    elements.completeModal.close()
+    renderLevelGrid()
+    updateCampaignUI()
+    openDialog(elements.levelModal)
+  })
+
+  document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeydown)
+
+  window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => {
+    saveSession()
+    saveProgress()
+  })
+
+  window.addEventListener('resize', () => board.resize())
+
+  // Native dialogs close with Escape, and the browser restores focus itself.
+  elements.completeModal.addEventListener('close', () => {
+    if (!completedThisAttempt) return
+    saveSession()
+  })
+}
+
+function boot() {
+  setSoundMuted(progress.muted)
+  bindEvents()
+  const saved = loadJSON(SESSION_KEY, null)
+  const savedLevel = Number(saved?.levelId)
+  const savedCompleted = Boolean(saved?.completed)
+  let launch = Number(progress.lastLevel) || 1
+  if (
+    saved &&
+    Number.isInteger(savedLevel) &&
+    savedLevel >= 1 &&
+    savedLevel <= LEVEL_COUNT &&
+    !savedCompleted &&
+    isUnlocked(savedLevel)
+  ) {
+    launch = savedLevel
+  }
+  if (!isUnlocked(launch)) launch = highestUnlocked()
+  setCurrentLevel(launch, { restore: !savedCompleted, saveCurrent: false })
+  requestAnimationFrame(frame)
+  window.setInterval(updateClock, 500)
+  updateCampaignUI()
+  renderLevelGrid()
+}
+
+boot()
+

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished browser logic puzzle game called **CIRCUIT MASTER** with functional electrical circuits, drag-and-drop wiring, 30 levels, hints/scoring, animations, progress saving, and responsive touch controls.

## Requirements
- Interactive circuit board with battery, wires, switches, LEDs, and logic gates.
- Drag-and-drop connections with genuine circuit validation.
- 30 progressively difficult levels.
- Hints and scoring.
- Animated electricity flow.
- Level selection and progress saving.
- Responsive mobile touch controls.
- User supplied a reference image of a neon black circuit board with luminous colored traces and components.

## Decisions
- Built as a static vanilla HTML/CSS/JS app, no build step.
- Implemented real graph simulation: battery high/ground rails, wire/switch nets, gate evaluation, LED anode/cathode validation, short/conflict detection, required-control checks, and gate input/output wiring requirements.
- Adopted a dark neon PCB visual language inspired by the reference image.
- Used Canvas for the board, real DOM for surrounding UI, native `<dialog>` for modals.
- Added tap-tap wiring fallback for mobile in addition to drag wiring.
- Levels store authored solution wires/switches for hints and automated tests; validation accepts any electrically valid circuit.
- Added component display scaling for sparse levels to make early puzzles look less empty.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created 30 authored levels with solutions in `js/levels.js`.
- Implemented circuit engine in `js/engine.js`.
- Implemented Canvas renderer in `js/board.js`.
- Implemented synthesized audio in `js/audio.js`.
- Created full UI structure in `index.html`.
- Created styling and responsive layouts in `styles.css`.
- Implemented game state, pointer wiring, hints, scoring, campaign map, completion modal, persistence, keyboard shortcuts, and touch behavior in `js/app.js`.
- Added automated engine tests in `tests/engine.test.mjs`; all 10 tests pass.
- Started local server in tmux session `circuit` on port 3000.
- Opened browser session `cm` and captured desktop screenshots.
- Fixed Playwright Chromium version mismatch by symlinking `chromium-1248` to `chromium-1243`.
- Fixed level 15 and 30 required-control mistakes; all authored solutions now validate.
- Added display scaling so early-level components are larger.

### Active
- Visual/gameplay verification in browser.
- Need to inspect actual wiring, solved state, animations, completion modal, level map, and mobile layout.
- Need favicon to eliminate the only console 404 (`/favicon.ico`).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Use Playwright to connect level 1’s four terminals and verify solved-state transition, animated wires, score, completion modal, and saved progress.
2. Inspect desktop screenshots after wiring and after completion; improve visual glow/density if needed.
3. Test level map modal, hint ghost wire, switch toggling, wire cutting/undo, and reset.
4. Test mobile viewport (390×844), including tap-tap wiring and responsive layout.
5. Add a favicon.
6. Run final tests and verify the generated `capture.sh` desktop/mobile screenshots.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/app.js`: main game state/UI/interactions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/engine.js`: circuit simulation and validation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/board.js`: Canvas rendering and hit testing.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/levels.js`: 30 levels, solutions, hints data.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: synthesized sound effects.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/desktop-2.png`: latest desktop screenshot.

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}

jobs:

# CIRCUIT MASTER

A neon logic-puzzle game about building real circuits. Thirty hand-built levels take you from a single lamp and cell to gated networks with switches, shared rails, and driver-conflict checks.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-single%20page-54f3ff?style=flat-square)
![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-vanilla%20ES%20modules-65ffad?style=flat-square)
![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/engine%20tests-10%20passing-ffc35f?style=flat-square)

## Play

The game is a static site with no build step. Serve the repository root:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3000
# or
npx serve .
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

## What is inside

- **A real circuit simulation** — batteries create high and ground rails; wires and closed switches form conductive nets; logic gates evaluate inputs; LEDs conduct anode to cathode and only into ground. Shorts, floating drivers, and conflicting gate outputs are rejected.
- **Thirty authored levels** across five chapters: Foundations, Gate Logic, Signal Theory, Networks, and Mastery.
- **Any valid solution** — progress validates the circuit itself, not a fixed list of wires.
- **Drag or tap wiring** — drag terminal to terminal on desktop; tap terminal A then terminal B on touch screens.
- **Animated current** — live traces pulse around a neon PCB with component glow, sparks, and synthesized audio.
- **Scoring and hints** — start at 1,000 points, spend 140 per hint, and earn up to three stars. Progress is saved to `localStorage`.
- **Campaign map, manual, and completion flow** — level unlocking, replay, score records, keyboard shortcuts, and a responsive layout down to phone widths.

## Controls

| Action | Input |
| --- | --- |
| Connect terminals | Drag, or tap one terminal then another |
| Toggle a switch | Click / tap it |
| Hint | `H` or the Hint button |
| Undo | `U` or the Undo button |
| Reset level | `R` or the Reset button |
| Cut mode | Cut button, then click a wire |
| Close a dialog | `Esc` |

## Tests

The engine and all authored solutions can be verified without a browser:

```bash
node --test tests/engine.test.mjs
```

The suite checks the 30-level catalogue, every authored solution, required controls, short detection, switch behavior, gate truth tables, duplicate wiring, and port geometry.

## Project layout

```text
index.html          App shell, HUD, dialogs
styles.css          Neon PCB design system and responsive layouts
js/app.js           Game state, pointer wiring, scoring, persistence
js/engine.js        Circuit graph simulation and validation
js/board.js         Canvas renderer, animation, and hit testing
js/levels.js        30 levels plus authored solutions and hints
js/audio.js         Synthesized Web Audio effects
tests/engine.test.mjs
```
